evidence: A person is sitting on the floor with legs extended, hands on the floor, and head tilted back, which matches the description of a person leaning backward with hands on the floor, extended legs or leaning against a wall do not by themselves mean lying or collapse. Ground lying requires human posture and ground-support evidence, not bounding-box proportions. Crawling and push-up/plank are supported on hands/knees/feet with the torso off the ground and are not high-priority ground lying. Work evidence must be visible tools/materials, repair/cleaning action, a dismantled/operated object or a clear person-to-work-object relationship. Proximity to equipment alone is insufficient. Work evidence applies only to that worker; it cannot negate a different person's lying/collapse signs. Lying on a bed or sofa is not ground lying. Do not infer a fall transition, cause, injury, consciousness, intent or danger.
